ko.label: Rule of law: courts subordinate to state security
ko.explanation: 2020 National Security Law and 2024 Article 23 ordinance: broadly drawn offences applying to any nationality, assets of suspects frozen with no time limit (US Hong Kong Business Advisory, September 2024); overseas judges including Lord Sumption resigned from the Court of Final Appeal in 2024; Freedom House 2026: 41/100, Partly Free. Commercial courts still function (WJP 2025: 24th of 143) and capital moves freely. See docs/research/china_hong_kong_foreign_wealth.md.

data.name: Hong Kong
data.summary: Hong Kong taxes individuals only on Hong Kong-source employment, business and property income. Capital gains and dividends (Hong Kong or foreign) received by an individual investor are not taxed, estate duty was abolished for deaths from 11 February 2006, and there is no gift or wealth tax. The residual costs are stamp duty (0.2% on Hong Kong share transfers, up to 6.5% on property), progressive government rates on homes, and the absence of a tax treaty with the US (US dividends bear 30% US withholding). The New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (HKD 30 million) is the main residence route for investors.

regimes.name: Ordinary residence
regimes.description: Territorial salaries/profits tax; passive investment income and gains of individuals are outside the charge.
regimes.eligibility: Any individual living in Hong Kong with a right to stay (New CIES, employment or dependant visa). Domestic liability does not depend on residence status.

capital_gains.summary: No capital gains tax. PwC: all capital gains derived by an individual are not subject to tax in Hong Kong. Gains that form part of a trade or business carried on in Hong Kong are taxed under profits tax.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Capital gains of any size are untaxed for a private investor.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Profits tax applies if an individual carries on a trade of dealing in securities or property in Hong Kong. Stamp duty of 0.2% of consideration (shared buyer/seller) applies to transfers of Hong Kong stock. Special and buyer's stamp duties on property were reduced to 0% from 28 February 2024.

sources.title: Hong Kong SAR - Individual - Income determination
Hong Kong SAR - Individual - Other taxes

capital_gains.rate_basis: Capital gains of individuals are outside the Inland Revenue Ordinance charge; 0% for a long-term private investor. Transaction stamp duty is not a gains tax and is excluded.
capital_gains.professional_trader: If the activity is a trade carried on in Hong Kong (frequent dealing with profit-seeking intent), the profits are assessable to profits tax. Badges-of-trade case law applies.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Gains on foreign assets are not taxed.

dividends.summary: Dividends derived by an individual are not taxed in Hong Kong, whether from Hong Kong or foreign companies. Foreign withholding tax is therefore a final cost.
dividends.important_exceptions: No treaty with the United States: US dividends bear 30% US withholding for a non-US person resident in Hong Kong. The FSIE regime (from 2023) applies to multinational-group entities, not to individuals.

sources.title: Hong Kong SAR - Individual - Income determination

dividends.rate_basis: Dividends are not chargeable to salaries, profits or property tax for an individual; 0%.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends or interest paid to non-residents.
dividends.treaty_network: 58 comprehensive treaties per PwC (7 pending ratification), mostly Asia/Europe; none with the United States. Hong Kong residence is only relevant for treaty access (ordinarily resident, more than 180 days in a year, or more than 300 days over two years).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Profits tax 16.5% (8.25% on the first HKD 2 million). A family-owned investment holding vehicle managed by an eligible single family office can be taxed at 0% on qualifying transactions (at least 2 full-time qualified employees and HKD 2 million of local operating expenditure).

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no levy on financial assets.

sources.title: Hong Kong SAR - Individual - Other taxes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Government rates on domestic property: 5% on the first HKD 550,000 of rateable value, 8% on the next HKD 250,000, 12% on the rest; plus government rent of 3% of rateable value on leased land. Property tax of 15% of net assessable value applies to let property only. Ad valorem stamp duty on purchases of residential property rises to 6.5% (above HKD 100 million).

inheritance.summary: No inheritance or gift tax. Estate duty was abolished by the Revenue (Abolition of Estate Duty) Ordinance 2005 with effect from 11 February 2006. Gifts of Hong Kong shares or property attract stamp duty on market value.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: No tax on inheritances or gifts of any amount.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Stamp duty on a gift (voluntary disposition inter vivos) of Hong Kong stock or property is charged on market value. Transfers on death by will or intestacy are not dutiable as gifts (general rule; not separately verified).

sources.title: Estate Duty
Hong Kong SAR - Individual - Other taxes

inheritance.gift_tax: None. Stamp duty applies to gifts of Hong Kong shares (0.2%) and Hong Kong property (ad valorem scale).

residency.tax_residency_test: Domestic tax liability does not depend on residence, domicile or citizenship. For treaty purposes an individual is resident if ordinarily residing in Hong Kong, or staying more than 180 days in a year of assessment or more than 300 days in two consecutive years.

routes.name: New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (New CIES)
routes.requirements: Net assets of at least HKD 30 million (from 1 March 2025 assessed over the 6 months before application, jointly owned family assets count pro rata) and investment of HKD 30 million in permissible Hong Kong assets within 6 months; can be held through a wholly owned private company including an FIHV. From 1 November 2026, only assets transacted through designated accounts count. Spouse and unmarried dependent children under 18 can accompany (general immigration rule; not verified here). The split between permissible assets, the CIES Investment Portfolio and real estate was not verified.

corporate.summary: Profits tax 16.5% (8.25% on the first HKD 2 million under the two-tier regime; one entity per connected group). Territorial: offshore profits are untaxed, but under the FSIE regime (from 2023, extended 2024) foreign dividends, interest and disposal gains received in Hong Kong by MNE group entities are taxed unless economic substance or participation requirements are met. Pillar Two: IIR and the Hong Kong minimum top-up tax apply from fiscal years beginning 1 January 2025. No dividend WHT.
corporate.special_zones: 0% for eligible family-owned investment holding vehicles (FIHV) managed by a Hong Kong single family office (from 1 April 2022); fund exemption for qualifying private funds (from 2019).

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain US-taxed on worldwide income; there is no US-Hong Kong income tax treaty, and Hong Kong levies nothing on investment income, so the US federal layer is the whole tax. An FIHV or Hong Kong company owned by a US person is likely a CFC/PFIC.

income.name: Hong Kong

income_tax.summary: Salaries tax is the lower of progressive rates (2% to 17%) on net chargeable income after the HKD 145,000 basic allowance (2026/27, up from HKD 132,000) and a standard rate of 15% on the first HKD 5 million of net income (16% above), so the effective top rate is 15%. Employees and the self-employed each pay 5% MPF capped at HKD 1,500 a month. Self-employed profits are under profits tax (7.5% to HKD 2m, then 15%) on a territorial basis, and fees for services performed in Hong Kong are Hong Kong-source.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed pay MPF at 5% of relevant income between HKD 7,100 and HKD 30,000 a month, maximum HKD 1,500 a month (HKD 18,000 a year). A sole trader pays profits tax, not salaries tax: 7.5% on the first HKD 2,000,000 of assessable profits and 15% above (IRD). Only profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong are taxed. Re-checked on the MPFA page on 2026-10-15: 5%, relevant income HKD 7,100 to 30,000 a month, maximum HKD 1,500 a month.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local or municipal income tax. The progressive schedule is capped by the standard rate: 15% on the first HKD 5,000,000 of net income (before personal allowances), 16% above, so the marginal rate paid by a high earner is effectively 15-16% rather than 17%. The brackets above are applied after the basic allowance. The 2026/27 basic allowance of HKD 145,000 (2025/26: HKD 132,000) is on the IRD 2026-27 Budget page, where the allowance measures are recorded as passed by LegCo on 13 May 2026 and gazetted on 22 May 2026; progressive rates are unchanged per secondary sources. Employment income: Hong Kong employment is taxable; for non-Hong Kong employment only services rendered in Hong Kong are taxed (time apportionment), ignoring visits of 60 days or fewer (PwC).

regimes.name: Top Talent Pass Scheme (TTPS)
regimes.description: Visa without a job offer for people with HKD 2.5m annual income in the year before applying (Category A) or a degree from a listed university plus 3 years of experience in the last five years (Category B), or a recent graduate (Category C, quota). It does not change tax: salaries tax follows the source of the employment income, not immigration status.
regimes.duration_note: Initial stay 36 months for Category A and 24 months for B and C; an extension is normally up to 3 years and is not guaranteed (ImmD), so 3+3 = 6 is used for Category A. A top-tier stream gives a six-year extension to holders with 2 years under the scheme and salaries tax income of HKD 2m or more.

sources.title: Hong Kong work and relocation visas 2026: GEP and Top Talent Pass

open_questions: Income test applies to Category A only; min_income left null because Categories B and C have none.

regimes.name: General Employment Policy (GEP)
regimes.description: Employer-sponsored work visa for professionals with a job offer that cannot readily be filled locally and market-rate pay. No special tax regime; standard salaries tax.
regimes.duration_note: Initial stay normally 36 months, extensions normally follow a 3-2 year pattern (ImmD), read here as 3+3+2 = 8 years. The ImmD page states a fixed HKD 2m salary only for the top-tier stream (2 years under GEP and salaries tax income of at least HKD 2m, five-year stay); the ordinary GEP has no salary figure beyond market rates.

open_questions: Whether the 3-2 pattern means 3+3+2 or 3+2 is read from one sentence on the ImmD page; 8 years assumed.

regimes.name: Territorial profits tax (offshore profits untaxed)
regimes.description: Profits tax applies only to profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong; profits earned abroad are not taxed even if remitted (IRD). It does not cover a contractor who does the work while living in Hong Kong: IRD Departmental Interpretation and Practice Notes No. 21 (revised) set the source of service fee income as the place where the services are performed, so fees earned by working in Hong Kong are Hong Kong-source and taxable, whoever the client is. The exemption only reaches fees for services performed outside Hong Kong.
regimes.duration_note: Permanent feature of the tax system, not a time-limited regime.

income.residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: no digital nomad visa was found. Skilled employees come through the General Employment Policy (job offer, market-rate pay, initial 36 months, extensions in a 3-2 pattern); high earners (HKD 2.5m the previous year) or graduates of listed universities with 3 years of experience can apply for the Top Talent Pass Scheme without a job offer (36 months for Category A, 24 for B and C). The Immigration Department pages do not distinguish nationalities; visa-free visitor stays do not allow local work.
